issues_found: The scenario as built depicts Marco Polo's 1271-1275 journey to Kublai Khan at Shangdu, not the Battle of Hastings (1066) at all
Player 1 is ITALIANS and Player 2 is MONGOLS; neither the Normans (Franks) nor the Anglo-Saxons (Britons) are present
No William of Normandy and no King Harold Godwinson; the KING unit is renamed 'Marco Polo' and a VILLAGER_MALE is 'Niccolo Polo'
Enemy force is CAVALRY_ARCHER x6, LIGHT_CAVALRY x4, SCOUT_CAVALRY -- Mongol steppe raiders, not an Anglo-Saxon infantry shield wall (no spearmen/militia mass, no hill defence)
Player force includes CAMEL_RIDER x3 as 'pack camels'; camels have no place at Hastings
Setting objects are Mongol/desert: YURT_A-D, PAVILION, TENT, TREE_PALM_FOREST, ROCK_FORMATION, gold mines -- not Sussex downland, Senlac Hill, or Norman/Saxon architecture
Victory is BRING_OBJECT_TO_AREA (King to Shangdu at 90,90), an escort objective; nothing about breaking a shield wall, killing Harold, or a nightfall deadline
Defeat triggers on loss of Marco Polo, Niccolo Polo, or pack camels -- caravan-escort losses unrelated to 1066
All in-game text narrates the Silk Road (1271, Khaidu's raiders, Kublai Khan), inventing a completely different event and period from the brief
strengths: Triggers are internally coherent and the escort narrative is consistently written, with staged waypoint dialogue and an ambush patrol event
Civilizations are explicitly assigned rather than left blank, and the Mongol assignment does at least match the (wrong) event depicted
justification: The built scenario has no relationship whatsoever to the Battle of Hastings: it is a Marco Polo Silk Road escort mission, with Italians versus Mongols, yurts and palm forests, a King renamed 'Marco Polo', and camel riders standing in for pack animals. Victory is reaching Shangdu at (90,90) and defeat is the loss of the Polos or their camels, none of which encodes William's assault on Harold's shield wall or the nightfall deadline the brief specifies. Every dimension fails at the floor, and a playthrough would teach the player about 1271-1275 Central Asia while being labelled 1066 England.

title: The Battle of Tours
objective_facts:
EXTRACTED VICTORY AND DEFEAT CONDITIONS
(taken directly from the trigger graph; score `objective` from
these, not from the objectives text)

Victory:
  - DESTROY_OBJECT on KING (player 2) [path "VC - Harold Slain"]
Defeat:
  - DESTROY_OBJECT on WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR (player 1) [path "Defeat - William Slain"]
  - TIMER on 1500s elapsed [path "Defeat - Nightfall"]
issues_found: The brief promises Charles Martel's Franks vs. Abd al-Rahman's Umayyads in 732, but the scenario as built is the Battle of Hastings 1066: William the Conqueror leads Player 1 and 'King Harold Godwinson' leads Player 2.

WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR is a hero from the wrong century (1066) and the wrong conflict entirely; Charles Martel has no engine hero but could have been represented by a renamed Frankish Throwing Axeman, Knight, or Champion.
Abd al-Rahman is entirely absent; Player 2 is instead an Anglo-Saxon king with Champions and Spearmen.
The Umayyad side is assigned BRITONS. The engine ships SARACENS (and Berbers in later editions), so an Islamic civilization for the invaders was available and its omission is avoidable.

Force composition is inverted: the Franks (Player 1) are given 10 Knights and 6 Light Cavalry as the attacking force, while the Umayyads (Player 2) are a static infantry force with 14 Spearmen and 6 Champions. Historically the Umayyads were the cavalry attackers and the Franks the infantry phalanx holding wooded high ground.
The promised third force of Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo does not exist — there are only two active players and no Odo unit, hero, or trigger.
No enemy camp exists to be struck; Player 2 has only a Town Center, Monastery, and three Houses.

Every line of in-game text narrates Hastings: 'October 14th, 1066', Senlac Hill, the shield wall, the fyrd, the feigned retreat, and the death of Harold. Nothing about Tours, Poitiers, Martel, or the Umayyads appears.
The 'feigned retreat' event trigger encodes a Norman tactic from Hastings, not any documented episode at Tours, where the Frankish line notably did NOT break.

Victory is gated on killing the enemy KING (Harold), whereas at Tours the Frankish objective was to hold the line and force the invaders' withdrawal; Abd al-Rahman's death was an outcome of the failed charges, not a target the Franks hunted.
Defeat on a 1500s nightfall timer is assigned to the wrong side: at Tours nightfall favoured the defenders (the Umayyads withdrew overnight), but here surviving to nightfall is a loss for the player.
strengths: Player 1 is assigned FRANKS, which is at least nominally the correct civilization for one side of Tours (though used here for Normans).
The map is heavily wooded (2400 oak trees), which is coincidentally consistent with the forested high ground the brief describes.

Victory and defeat conditions are both cleanly implemented and hinge on named leader figures rather than total annihilation, showing the trigger craft is competent even though aimed at the wrong battle.
justification: This is not a scenario about the Battle of Tours at all; it is a complete Hastings 1066 scenario with a Tours label pasted on. William the Conqueror stands in the field, Harold Godwinson holds Senlac Hill, the dialogue is dated 'October 14th, 1066', and the scripted turning point is the Norman feigned retreat luring the fyrd off the slope — 334 years and an entirely different conflict away from Charles Martel and Abd al-Rahman. The promised Umayyad cavalry, Aquitanian allies under Duke Odo, and enemy camp are all absent, and the roles are inverted so the 'Frankish' player attacks with ten Knights while the enemy holds with spearmen. The encoded goal (slay the enemy king before a nightfall deadline that penalises the defender) is the opposite of the historical Frankish task of holding ground until the invaders withdrew, and a player would come away with a confidently false picture of 732.

issues_found: The scenario as built depicts the Battle of Hastings (1066), not the Battle of Tours (732): every line of narration names Duke William, Harold Godwinson, Senlac Hill and the Anglo-Saxon shield wall.

WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR is placed as the player's hero in place of Charles Martel — a figure from the wrong culture (Norman) and wrong century (334 years later). The engine ships no Martel hero, but a renamed generic Frankish unit (or even Charlemagne) would have been the correct substitution; this is avoidable error.
Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi is entirely absent; the enemy commander is a generic KING renamed Harold Godwinson, an Anglo-Saxon king with no connection to the Umayyad invasion.
Player 2 is assigned BRITONS — Anglo-Saxon architecture and roster — for what should be an Umayyad/Berber force. The engine offers Saracens or Berbers, so this is avoidable.

Force composition is inverted: the player (nominally the Franks) fields 10 KNIGHTS and 6 LIGHT_CAVALRY, while the enemy is 14 SPEARMEN and 6 CHAMPIONS. At Tours the Franks were the dense infantry phalanx and the Umayyads the heavy cavalry; here the roles are reversed.
The third force of Aquitanians under Duke Odo promised in the brief has no player slot, no units, and no rally trigger — there are only two active players.
No enemy camp exists to strike; the Umayyad baggage camp, whose defence reportedly broke the invaders' cohesion, is unrepresented.
The 'feigned retreat' trigger and the 'fyrd breaks ranks' event are Hastings tactics; nothing in the sources for Tours describes them.

Victory/defeat roles are reversed: the Franks were the defenders who had only to hold the high ground, yet here the timer expiring (holding until nightfall) is a DEFEAT for the player, and victory requires slaying the enemy leader as an attacker.
strengths: Player 1 is at least assigned FRANKS, which is the correct civilization for Charles Martel's army, even if the roster attached to it is Norman cavalry.
The map is heavily wooded (2400 oak trees), which is loosely consistent with the wooded terrain the brief describes between Tours and Poitiers.
The enemy commander's death as the victory trigger coincidentally parallels Abd al-Rahman's death in the actual battle, though the object is named Harold Godwinson.
justification: This is not a scenario about Tours at all: the placed hero is William the Conqueror, the enemy is a Briton king renamed Harold Godwinson, and every narration line describes Senlac Hill on 14 October 1066. The historical relationship is also inverted — the Franks' defensive infantry wall becomes a cavalry-and-archer assault force, the Umayyad horsemen become an Anglo-Saxon spear line, and Duke Odo's Aquitanian third force and the Umayyad camp are absent entirely. The encoded conditions make outlasting the day a defeat, when holding the field until the invaders withdrew was precisely the Frankish victory condition. A player would come away with a confident, detailed, and entirely false picture of what the brief claims to teach.

title: The Exile of El Cid
objective_facts:
EXTRACTED VICTORY AND DEFEAT CONDITIONS
(taken directly from the trigger graph; score `objective` from
these, not from the objectives text)

Victory:
  - DESTROY_OBJECT on CAVALIER (player 2) [path "Victory - Abd al-Rahman Slain"]
Defeat:
  - DESTROY_OBJECT on CHAMPION (player 1) [path "Defeat - Martel Slain"]
  - OBJECTS_IN_AREA on count 6, player 2, area (48,10)-(72,26) [path "Defeat - Ridge Overrun"]
issues_found: El Cid (Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar) does not appear anywhere in the scenario, despite the engine shipping a dedicated El Cid hero unit — an entirely avoidable omission for a scenario titled 'The Exile of El Cid'.
Player 1's leader is a CHAMPION renamed 'Charles Martel', a Frankish figure of 732, roughly 350 years before the events in the brief.
Player 2's leader is a CAVALIER renamed 'Abd al-Rahman' (Al Ghafiqi, the Umayyad commander at Tours), not a taifa ruler such as al-Muqtadir/al-Musta'in of Zaragoza or al-Qadir of Valencia.

'Duke Odo' of Aquitaine is summoned as a reinforcement — another eighth-century figure irrelevant to eleventh-century Iberia; King Alfonso VI of Castile, the actual antagonist of the exile, is absent.
Player 1 is assigned FRANKS rather than SPANISH, though the engine offers a Spanish civilization with Iberian architecture appropriate to Castile and Valencia.
The map is 2,218 oak trees forming a 'wooded ridge between Poitiers and Tours' — northern French forest, not the Ebro valley, the Levantine huerta, or the meseta of the Iberian campaigns.

No siege of Valencia, no service under Zaragoza against Aragon/Barcelona, no growing retinue mechanic; the scenario contains no Spanish or Muslim-Iberian settlement at all (only Saracen tents, a pavilion and a market as a 'plunder camp').
Victory is gated on killing the CAVALIER 'Abd al-Rahman'; the brief's culminating act — taking Valencia in his own name — is not encoded as any condition.
Defeat on six Player 2 units entering a ridge area (48,10)-(72,26) encodes a static defensive line battle, the opposite of El Cid's mobile mercenary campaigning and offensive conquest.
The defeat-on-leader-death trigger fires on the CHAMPION renamed Charles Martel, so even the one mechanic the brief specifies ('losing El Cid himself means defeat') is attached to the wrong person.
Every line of in-game text dates the action to 'October, 732 AD' and states 'Tours is saved', misdating the brief's 1081-1094 by three and a half centuries.
strengths: The scenario is internally coherent as a Battle of Tours map: Frankish infantry on a wooded ridge, Umayyad cavalry (camel riders, cavalry archers, knights) charging in three timed waves, a flanking Aquitanian raid on the baggage camp, and withdrawal on the emir's death all match the sources for 732.
Diplomacy is explicitly set by trigger and both active players have assigned civilizations rather than being left default.
justification: The built scenario is not the claimed event at all: it is a Battle of Tours (732) map, complete with Charles Martel, Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi, Duke Odo of Aquitaine, a wooded Poitiers ridge of 2,218 oaks, and narration explicitly dated 'October, 732 AD'. El Cid himself is absent even though the engine ships an El Cid hero, the Spanish civilization that would suit Castile and Valencia is replaced by Franks, and neither Zaragozan service nor the conquest of Valencia appears in the roster or triggers. The encoded goal — slay the Umayyad emir, do not let six horsemen reach the Frankish camp — is the objective of a defensive battle in Gaul, not of a mercenary's exile campaign in Iberia, and a playthrough would teach the player nothing true about 1081-1094.

issues_found: The scenario depicts the Battle of Tours (732 AD) rather than El Cid's exile (1081-1094): all narration, triggers and named figures are Charles Martel, Duke Odo and Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi.

Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar is entirely absent. The engine ships a dedicated El Cid hero unit (and Alfonso/Motamid-adjacent options), so casting a renamed Champion as 'Charles Martel' instead is wholly avoidable error.

King Alfonso VI of Castile, the Muslim king of Zaragoza (al-Mu'tamin) and the Almoravids/Berenguer Ramon II are all missing; the opposing side is an 8th-century Umayyad raiding host of camel riders and cavalry archers.

Player 1 is FRANKS with Town Center, Barracks, Monastery and Houses: Frankish (Western European) architecture, not the Iberian/Spanish civilisation the brief requires; the Spanish civ exists in the engine.
Terrain is 2,218 oak trees forming a wooded ridge between Poitiers and Tours; nothing resembles the Ebro valley, Zaragoza, or the walled city of Valencia the brief names as the campaign's climax.
Victory condition is DESTROY_OBJECT on a Cavalier renamed 'Abd al-Rahman', i.e. slaying an 8th-century emir, rather than the siege and capture of Valencia in 1094.
Defeat condition triggers on the death of the Champion renamed 'Charles Martel', not on the loss of El Cid as the brief explicitly states.
The second defeat condition (6 enemy units reaching a camp area) encodes a defensive ridge-holding action; El Cid's exile years were offensive mercenary campaigning, not a static defence.

The player's force is 18 Spearmen, 16 Skirmishers and 6 Men-at-Arms on foot: El Cid's fame rested on a mounted retinue of Castilian knights, and the brief's 'small retinue grows through victories' mechanic is nowhere implemented.
The 'plunder camp burns and horsemen desert' turning point is a Tours-tradition episode with no relation to Zaragoza, Almenar, Tevar, or Cuarte.
strengths: The scenario is internally coherent and technically competent for the event it actually builds: dated narration, three timed cavalry waves, a flag-triggered flanking reinforcement, and matching victory/defeat text.

Franks-versus-Saracens with spear infantry holding wooded terrain against cavalry is a defensible representation of the 732 engagement it depicts, and the leaders of that battle are correctly named via CHANGE_OBJECT_NAME.
justification: This scenario has no relationship whatever to the brief it claims: instead of Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar's 1081-1094 exile, mercenary service to Zaragoza, and conquest of Valencia, the built content is the Battle of Tours in October 732, with Charles Martel (a renamed Champion), Duke Odo, and Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi named explicitly in the narration and trigger names. The victory condition kills an 8th-century Umayyad commander and the defeat condition fires on Martel's death, not El Cid's, despite the brief stating that losing El Cid means defeat; the engine ships an El Cid hero and a Spanish civilisation, so both the casting and the Frankish Town Center/Monastery architecture on a 2,218-tree Poitiers ridge are avoidable errors. A playthrough would teach the player about Tours while being labelled as El Cid's exile, which is actively misleading about both events.

title: The Fall of Constantinople
objective_facts:
EXTRACTED VICTORY AND DEFEAT CONDITIONS
(taken directly from the trigger graph; score `objective` from

Victory:
  - DESTROY_OBJECT on CASTLE (player 2) [path "[VC] Valencia Falls"]
Defeat:
  - DESTROY_OBJECT on EL_CID (player 1) [path "[Defeat] El Cid Falls"]
issues_found: The scenario depicts the campaigns of El Cid (1081-1094), not the 1453 siege of Constantinople; not one element of the brief appears.

Player 1 is led by EL_CID, a Castilian hero from the 11th century, standing in for Constantine XI — a figure of the wrong culture and nearly four centuries out of period, and avoidable since the engine ships no Palaiologos hero but does allow a renamed generic unit (and Constantine's Byzantine roster exists).
Player 1 is assigned SPANISH rather than BYZANTINES; Player 2 is SARACENS rather than TURKS, so architecture and unit sets are wrong for both besieger and defender.

Mehmed II and the Ottoman army are absent entirely; the attacker fields CAMEL_RIDER, KNIGHT, SKIRMISHER and CHAMPION with no bombard cannons, janissary-equivalents, or any siege train — the defining artillery of 1453 is nowhere in the roster.

The defender has no fortifications at all: the 40 STONE_WALL segments, CASTLE, GATE and 4 GUARD_TOWERs all belong to Player 2, the attacker, so the Theodosian Walls the player is told to hold do not exist on the player's side.
No Golden Horn, sea walls, harbour, or Hagia Sophia district is represented; there is no water feature or landmark building of any kind, and no repair-breach or naval mechanic.
Victory is DESTROY_OBJECT on the enemy CASTLE ('the Alcazar of Valencia') — an offensive conquest goal, the exact inverse of a defender surviving a siege.
Defeat is the death of EL_CID rather than the fall of the Hagia Sophia district or the collapse of the walls.

All in-game text narrates Alfonso VI's banishment, service to Zaragoza, Tevar 1090 and Valencia 1094 — a playthrough would teach the player nothing about 1453 and would actively contradict the stated title.
strengths: The scenario is internally coherent as a piece of design (dated narration, staged trigger progression, escalating objectives), even though it depicts a completely different event.
justification: This is an El Cid campaign scenario mislabelled as the Fall of Constantinople: the narration covers 1081-1094 in Iberia, the player hero is EL_CID, and the civilizations are Spanish versus Saracens rather than Byzantines versus Turks. Every specific element of the brief — Constantine XI, Mehmed II, bombard-created breaches, the Theodosian and sea walls, the Golden Horn, the Hagia Sophia district — is absent, and the only walls and towers on the map belong to the enemy. The encoded goal (destroy the enemy Castle, lose if El Cid dies) inverts the historical situation of a defender who needed only to outlast the assault. Nothing here can be attributed to engine limitation: Byzantines, Turks, bombard cannons, and long stone wall lines are all available.

justification: This scenario does not depict the Fall of Constantinople in any respect: it is an El Cid campaign mission, with SPANISH versus SARACENS, the hero EL_CID standing where Constantine XI should be, and narration covering 1081–1094 in Iberia. The defining features of the brief — the Theodosian Walls, Ottoman bombards, the Golden Horn sea walls, the Hagia Sophia district — are wholly absent, and the only walls on the map belong to the enemy. The encoded goal (destroy the enemy CASTLE, lose if EL_CID dies) is the precise inversion of a defensive siege the Byzantines needed only to outlast, and a playthrough would teach the player nothing true about 1453.

issues_found: The brief calls for Mongols (Temujin's warband) versus rival steppe tribes (Merkits, Jamukha's Jadaran, Naimans); the scenario assigns Player 1 BYZANTINES and Player 2 TURKS — neither the Mongol nor any steppe-appropriate civilization (Mongols, Tatars, Cumans, Huns) was used, though the engine ships all of them.

Named characters are Constantine XI, Mehmed II and Giovanni Giustiniani, figures of 1453 Constantinople — roughly 250 years and 5,000 km removed from Temujin, Borte, Jamukha and Toghrul. Temujin himself, the protagonist, does not appear in any form; the player's leader is a KING renamed 'Constantine XI'.

Force composition is entirely wrong for the steppe: 10 SPEARMEN, 10 ARCHERS, 6 CROSSBOWMEN and a CHAMPION behind 78 STONE_WALL tiles for the player, versus KNIGHTS, CAVALIER and three BOMBARD_CANNON for the enemy. Mongol warfare of 1186-1206 was overwhelmingly horse-archer based; gunpowder artillery is a flat anachronism for 1206.
